title: String Calculator Negative Diagnostic Contract
summary: Preserves the exact Python and command-line negative-number diagnostic behavior.
problem_statement: A structured Specification must retain the complete observable source contract without weakening equality, ordering, duplication, separators, streams, status, or newlines.

items.title: Python rejection error type and text
items.statement: The public add operation MUST raise ValueError whose complete message equals `negative numbers not allowed: ` followed by every canonical negative value in encounter order, separated by comma and space, with duplicate occurrences preserved.
items.rationale: Python callers need the complete source-defined rejection diagnostic.
acceptance: Input `-01,2,-003,-01` raises ValueError with complete message `negative numbers not allowed: -1, -3, -1`.
The message contains no additional prefix, suffix, or text.

source_notes.text: The source requires the complete diagnostic, every canonical negative in encounter order, comma-space separators, and preserved duplicates.

items.title: Installed command with positional input
items.statement: The project MUST install a string-calculator command that accepts one Number List as a positional argument for supported invocations.
acceptance: The string-calculator executable is available after project installation.
A supported invocation supplies one Number List positional argument.

items.title: CLI successful output contract
items.statement: On successful calculation the installed command MUST write only the decimal sum and one trailing newline to standard output, write nothing to standard error, and exit zero.
acceptance: A successful invocation for `1,2` writes exactly `3` followed by one newline to standard output.
The invocation writes nothing to standard error and exits zero.

items.title: CLI negative rejection contract
items.statement: On negative-number rejection the installed command MUST write the Python error text and one trailing newline to standard error, write no sum to standard output, and exit nonzero.
acceptance: An invocation containing `-1` writes `negative numbers not allowed: -1` followed by one newline to standard error.
The rejected invocation writes no sum to standard output and exits nonzero.
